chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Rahman, from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): Inform me about the best times for the Fajr prayer.
He said: 'With the rising of dawn. Indeed, Allāh the Exalted says: "Indeed, the Quran of dawn is witnessed." He means the Fajr prayer; the angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it.
So when the servant prays the dawn prayer with the rising of dawn, it is recorded for him twice; the angels of the night and the angels of the day record it for him.'

key_terms.قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ: The Quran of dawn (referring to the Fajr prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the best time to pray Fajr and why is it rewarded twice?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* highlights the theological significance of the Fajr prayer as the unique moment where the angels of the night (who record deeds during darkness) and the angels of the day (who record during light) converge to witness the worshipper, thereby doubling the reward. It underscores the Shia emphasis on precise timing (waqt) in prayer, linking the physical act of worship to the cosmic order of angelic testimony mentioned in Surah Al-Isra. This dual witnessing serves as a spiritual incentive for believers to prioritize the early morning prayer amidst the transition from night to day.
